templates.name: Static Site Generation Success
templates.description: Verify that the build tool successfully ingests a representative folder of Markdown notes and produces a complete static site (HTML/CSS/JS/assets) without errors. Confirm the output directory contains all expected files and the site is browsable locally or via static hosting.

templates.name: Full-Text Search Accuracy
templates.description: Test full-text search by executing a predefined set of queries (at least 10 representative queries) against the generated site. Measure precision: each query must return the expected target note within the top 10 results. Verify search index is generated at build time and queries execute client-side without backend.

templates.name: Tag Extraction and Navigation
templates.description: Verify that all tags defined in notes (via the agreed representation: frontmatter, inline, or both) are correctly extracted and indexed. Confirm that tag pages/filters are generated and that navigating to a tag displays all notes with that tag. Test with a dataset covering single tags, multiple tags per note, and notes without tags.

templates.name: Forward Links and Backlinks Rendering
templates.description: Test link detection and backlink computation by creating a test dataset with known link relationships (using the agreed Markdown/wiki-link syntax). Verify that forward links render correctly in each note and that backlinks sections list all notes linking to the current note. Confirm 100% accuracy on the test dataset.

templates.name: Markdown Formatting Preservation
templates.description: Verify that the generated site preserves Markdown formatting and structure (headings, lists, code blocks, emphasis, images, etc.) as rendered HTML. Test with a representative sample of Markdown features and confirm visual and semantic correctness in the output.

templates.name: Static Hosting Verification
templates.description: Deploy the generated static site to a chosen static hosting platform (e.g., GitHub Pages, Netlify) or serve locally via a static file server. Confirm that all core features (browsing, search, tags, links, backlinks) function correctly without requiring server-side runtime or database.

templates.name: Cross-Browser Compatibility
templates.description: Open the generated site in modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) and verify that all features (navigation, search, tags, links, backlinks) work without errors or visual issues. Test on a representative dataset.

templates.name: Performance and Scale Validation
templates.description: Measure site generation time and search responsiveness on a representative dataset (e.g., 100+ notes). Confirm that performance meets agreed targets (to be defined once scale and targets are clarified). Record baseline metrics for future comparison.

templates.name: Link Syntax Handling
templates.description: Test the tool with the agreed Markdown flavor and link syntax (e.g., CommonMark/GFM, standard Markdown links, [[WikiLinks]]). Verify correct parsing, rendering, and backlink computation for all supported link formats. Confirm unsupported formats are handled gracefully (ignored or flagged).

templates.name: Tag Representation Handling
templates.description: Test tag extraction and rendering using the agreed tag representation (YAML frontmatter, inline #tags, or both). Verify correct parsing, indexing, and navigation. If nested tags are supported, confirm hierarchy is preserved.

templates.name: Build Workflow and Environment
templates.description: Verify that the build tool runs successfully in the target OS environments (to be specified) and supports the preferred workflow (CLI, watch mode, git-based build). Confirm installation, configuration, and execution steps are documented and repeatable.

templates.name: Input File Assumptions
templates.description: Confirm that the tool correctly reads Markdown files from a local filesystem or repository as input. Test with various directory structures, file encodings, and edge cases (empty files, missing frontmatter, special characters in filenames).

coverage_guidance: Ensure acceptance tests cover all success metrics (SM1-SM7) with measurable pass criteria.
Test both happy path (valid inputs, expected usage) and edge cases (empty notes, malformed Markdown, missing links/tags, large datasets).
Validate constraints CNS1 and CNS2: output must be static and input must be standard Markdown.
Confirm all high-impact assumptions (A1-A4) are testable once open questions (Q1, Q2) are resolved.
Include tests for non-goals to verify they are explicitly NOT implemented (e.g., no server-side runtime, no real-time editing).
Test interoperability: generated site must work across target browsers and hosting platforms.
Performance tests should establish baseline metrics and be repeatable as the project scales.

Acceptance tests should be automatable where possible (build success, link/backlink accuracy, tag extraction) and include manual verification steps where needed (visual rendering, cross-browser checks).
definition_of_done: All acceptance test templates (ATT1-ATT12) have been executed with documented results.
Success metrics SM1-SM7 are met with measurable evidence.
High-impact open questions Q1 and Q2 are resolved and corresponding tests (ATT9, ATT10) pass.
Generated static site is deployable to target hosting platform and functions without server-side dependencies.
Core features (search, tags, links, backlinks, Markdown rendering) are verified on a representative dataset.
Cross-browser compatibility is confirmed for all target browsers.
Performance baseline is established for generation time and search responsiveness on agreed dataset scale.
All constraints (CNS1, CNS2) are satisfied and validated.
Non-goals (NG1-NG7) are confirmed as out-of-scope and not implemented.
Documentation includes setup, build, and deployment instructions verified via ATT11.
Any deviations from success metrics or unresolved blocking questions are explicitly documented and approved by stakeholders.
